package_info.package_name: polyfill.io (CDN service, as used by npm packages such as create-polyfill-service-url and dynamic-polyfill)
package_info.package_manager: npm (and any web project embedding the CDN)
package_info.package_versions: All versions using cdn.polyfill.io after domain ownership change (February 2024 onward)
package_info.why_malicious: The polyfill.io CDN began serving malicious JavaScript after a change in domain ownership. The CDN injected code that redirected mobile users to scam sites, affecting any website or npm package embedding scripts from cdn.polyfill.io. This constitutes a supply chain attack, as the malicious code was automatically deployed to all dependent sites and packages.

execution_context.trigger: runtime (when a user visits a website embedding the CDN script)
execution_context.file_location: Served JavaScript from cdn.polyfill.io (injected into web pages via <script src="https://cdn.polyfill.io/v3/polyfill.min.js"></script>)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code checks if the visitor is using a mobile device by inspecting the user agent string, then redirects the browser to a scam site, resulting in user redirection and potential phishing or fraud.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code performs user agent detection and forcibly redirects users to an external, attacker-controlled domain, which is not expected behavior for a polyfill library.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: A polyfill service should only provide compatibility code for older browsers, not perform user agent checks for malicious redirection.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: User agent checks and redirection may be used for mobile site optimization or A/B testing, but never in a polyfill CDN context.
key_indicators: User agent sniffing for mobile devices
Forced redirection to external, non-affiliated domains
Injected into all sites using the CDN, not just a single application

attack_chain.action: Website or npm package embeds the polyfill.io CDN script.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious JavaScript is loaded into the user's browser.

attack_chain.action: Malicious JavaScript executes in the browser context.
attack_chain.leads_to: Checks if the visitor is on a mobile device.

attack_chain.action: If on mobile, user is redirected to a scam site.
attack_chain.leads_to: User is exposed to phishing, fraud, or further malware.

behavioral_signatures: Polyfill CDN script performing user agent checks and redirection
Unexpected network requests to scam or non-polyfill domains from polyfill scripts
Polyfill scripts containing obfuscated or non-polyfill logic
file_indicators: Any JavaScript file loaded from cdn.polyfill.io after February 2024
network_indicators: Outbound requests or redirects to domains unrelated to polyfill.io (e.g., scam-landing pages)
Any HTTP(S) requests initiated by polyfill scripts to attacker-controlled infrastructure
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for websites or npm packages loading scripts from cdn.polyfill.io, especially if the script performs user agent checks and redirects users to external domains. Use Content Security Policy (CSP) violation reports to detect unexpected script sources or redirections. Analyze loaded polyfill scripts for non-standard logic, such as DOM manipulation or network requests unrelated to polyfill functionality. Flag any polyfill CDN usage after the domain's change of ownership as high risk.
